newsitem.title: SPAIN: Telefonica lower, still outperforming Ibex.
newsitem.headline: Telefonica lower, still outperforming Ibex.

text.p: Shares in Spain's Telefonica were lower on Friday but still outperforming the broad share indices on strong retail demand amid the placement of the government's 20.9 percent stake in the firm.
But traders said they were doubtful that the institutional tranche of the offer would be as popular, simply because the share price is thought to be too high.
At 1255 GMT Telefonica was down 45 pesetas, or 1.33 percent, to 3,335, while the Ibex-35 index of leading shares was down 1.88 percent to 5,348.41.
"The retail tranche seems to be going well, although it looks like the subscription figures are exaggerated a little," said a trader at a foreign brokerage.

But a second trader said that, if anything, the managers of the sale were trying to tone down reports of the strong retail demand, aiming to provoke the interest of domestic and foreign funds who are concerned at the high price of the sale.

"The shares have had support in the run-up to the sale, and the retail segment has done well. But the institutions are not so convinced. (The shares) might prove difficult to place with those outside the lead-managers' immediate circle," he said.
The final price of the stock will be set on February 17.
